subject: Resiliency review & next steps — failover, rate limits, and comparative tests
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Resiliency review & next steps — failover, rate limits, and comparative tests

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single plan to validate reliability and operational behavior versus the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned. Key takeaways from the demo/discovery:

- Your priority metrics: sustained 99.95% uptime, mean 95th-latency < 180ms for request sizes typical of inference calls, and predictable burst handling during nightly batch windows.
- Competitive signals: Orbital's infra team has seen lower tail-latency variance on MajorCloud but higher throttling during medium bursts; FastServe was aggressive on token pricing but had longer cold-start variability.
- Compliance note: you need evidence of failover behavior (multi-region + model fallback) and an error-budget report for the last rolling 30 days.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Redwood will run a focused failover & burst test against our hosted API and a pinned model variant to show: graceful degradation, failover latency, request loss rate, and cache warm-up characteristics.
2) We will share a short runbook (failover scenarios, exact endpoints, and payloads) and a CSV baseline of our performance numbers.
3) We suggest a 60-minute ops deep-dive next Wed (Apr 22) 10:30–11:30 PT with your infra lead to walk through the test harness and expected artifact outputs.

Deliverables we will produce: runbook PDF, perf baseline CSV, a short doc summarizing error budget math and SLO assumptions.

If that plan looks good I’ll finalize the runbook and trigger the tests. Also attaching a request — could you share the traffic profile CSV you mentioned so we can align load shapes?

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: proposed test plan (will send), request for traffic profile
From: Sara Patel <sara@orbitalai.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orbital AI Engineering Team <infra@orbitalai.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Resiliency review & next steps — failover, rate limits, and comparative tests

Thanks Dylan — that recap is exactly right. Quick responses and additions:

- Confirmed: MajorCloud and FastServe are the two finalists we are comparing you against. We care most about degraded-mode behavior (how the API responds when a single AZ goes down and when rate limits are hit) because our app must stay online for enterprise customers.
- Request: can you include a test that simulates an AZ outage and a regional failover (multi-region redirect) and show request success rate and tail-latency before/after?
- For rate limits, we need to see: throttling thresholds, behavior when token/req quotas are exceeded (429 vs queued vs dropped), and the length of token bucket refill windows.

I attached the traffic profile (orbital-traffic-profile.csv) we discussed — it includes 1-week representative traffic with peak/burst windows.

We can do the Wed 10:30 PT slot. I’ll bring our infra lead (Carlos) and one platform engineer.

Also: do you have comparisons (one-pagers) showing Redwood vs MajorCloud on failover and error-budget handling? That helps our procurement folks.

—Sara
Head of Platform — Orbital AI
Attachments: orbital-traffic-profile.csv
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Resiliency review & next steps — failover, rate limits, and comparative tests

Looping in the reliability team items and proposed test matrix. Draft test plan highlights:

- Test matrix: 1) AZ outage simulation (cut traffic to one AZ), 2) regional failover (redirect to secondary region), 3) sustained burst (5x baseline for 10m), 4) token-exceed scenario (step up requests until throttling observed).
- Metrics to capture: request success rate, 99/95/50 latency percentiles, 429/5xx counts, cache hit ratio, time-to-kv-cache-warm after failover, and queue length over time.
- Failure criteria: any percent-loss >0.5% during failover window flagged; tail-latency degradation above 2x baseline flagged.

Marissa — will you own running the AZ/regional failover run and produce the baseline CSV? Dylan — can you send Sara the Redwood failover runbook PDF and the HubSpot link to the deal? I’ll prep the test harness and confirm endpoints.

Action items:
- Marissa: run AZ/regional failover tests Tue evening and capture output (redwood-performance-baseline.csv).
- Dylan: share runbook PDF + schedule invite with meeting link for Wed 10:30 PT.
- Neha: configure the burst/429 scenario in the harness and produce graphs.

Thanks —
Neha
Director, Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Resiliency review & next steps — failover, rate limits, and comparative tests

Sara — thanks, all set on our side. Attached are the two artifacts we promised: redwood-failover-runbook.pdf and a preliminary redwood-performance-baseline.csv. High level notes:

- Failover behavior: our multi-region routing triggers model-fallback within 6–8s in the tested scenario; we keep in-flight requests routed to the secondary region rather than dropping in our default configuration. Failure alpha: in-work requests may see tail-latency spikes up to ~2.3x for <20s as KV cache re-warms (we show this in the baseline CSV).
- Rate limiting: Redwood enforces soft queueing up to configured burst windows; after that we return 429 with an x-retry-after header. In tests we observed queued requests being drained within 30s for bursts 3x baseline, and token refill windows are linear (configurable per account). We’ll show the exact thresholds in the ops session.
- Competitive notes: MajorCloud showed slightly lower cold-cache tail-latency in our internal synthetic tests but their behavior under burst token-exhaustion was to immediately return 429 without soft queueing; FastServe had higher nominal throughput but longer geo-failover latencies in our runs.

Next: I scheduled the ops deep-dive for Wed Apr 22 10:30–11:30 PT (calendar invite sent). Meeting link and HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/Orbital-AI/record/6723

Attachments: redwood-failover-runbook.pdf, redwood-performance-baseline.csv

Best,
Dylan

See you Wed.
